test_cases.title: Four concurrent ingest-triggered rebuilds on distinct programs succeed with zero IntegrityError and match serial output
test_cases.given: Four ingest-triggered rebuilds for four distinct programs are queued, each running rebuild_program_rollups(program_id) then rebuild_org_rollups() on its own AsyncSession against a shared migrated test-Postgres
test_cases.when: all four call-pairs execute concurrently via asyncio.gather
test_cases.then: all four complete successfully with zero IntegrityError on org_summary_rollup_org_id_key, and the resulting org_summary_rollup/token_series/mau_series rows equal a serial rebuild over the same usage_events content
test_cases.objective: Verify the org-singleton concurrency fix lets four concurrent ingest-triggered rebuilds on distinct programs all succeed with zero IntegrityError, and that the concurrently-produced rollup rows are identical to a serial rebuild's output.
preconditions: services/api/tests/conftest.py migrated_db fixture applied (upgrade head) against the real test-Postgres instance
usage_events seeded with events for exactly four distinct program_ids (program-1..program-4), each with a non-trivial row count
org_summary_rollup pre-populated with an existing singleton row for org_id='org-1' (reproduces the DELETE+INSERT collision window from docs/research/ING-02.md)
New four-session concurrency fixture (FR-4) available in or alongside conftest.py, each program pinned to its own AsyncSession

test_data.concurrency_mechanism_under_test: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (decision of record) or pg_advisory_xact_lock (fallback), whichever /arh-plan-implementation confirms

steps: Seed usage_events for program-1..program-4 (500 rows each) plus a pre-existing org_summary_rollup singleton row for org_id=org-1
Capture a serial-rebuild baseline: run rebuild_program_rollups + rebuild_org_rollups sequentially for each program on one session, snapshot org_summary_rollup/token_series/mau_series
Reset rollup tables to their pre-rebuild state
Launch four concurrent tasks via asyncio.gather, each on its own AsyncSession, each calling rebuild_program_rollups(program_id) then rebuild_org_rollups() for one of the four programs
Await all four tasks and collect results/exceptions
Query org_summary_rollup, token_series, mau_series after all four tasks complete
Diff the concurrently-produced rows against the serial-rebuild baseline snapshot from step 2
Inspect the rollup_rebuild_completed log emitted for each call pair for the contention_wait_ms field
expected_results: All four tasks complete with a RebuildResult returned; none raises IntegrityError on org_summary_rollup_org_id_key
org_summary_rollup contains exactly one row for org_id=org-1, matching the serial-rebuild baseline on every column except id/as_of_timestamp/created_at/updated_at
token_series and mau_series rows after concurrent execution match the serial-rebuild baseline row-for-row on every column except the excluded id/clock columns
Each call pair's rollup_rebuild_completed log entry includes a non-negative integer contention_wait_ms, present even when 0

test_cases.title: Rebuild duration holds flat against table size across >=2 populated usage_events sizes (growth-curve regression guard)
test_cases.given: test_rollup_rebuild_perf.py seeds a populated, growing usage_events table at >=2 of {20k, 40k, 160k} total rows, replacing the empty-table EVENT_COUNT=5000/BUDGET_SECONDS=2.0 constants
test_cases.when: rebuild_org_rollups() and rebuild_program_rollups(program_id) each run once per seeded table size
test_cases.then: each function's duration is asserted against a pinned per-table-size budget constant and the curve stays flat rather than tracking table growth, per docs/research/ING-02.md's measured baseline (rebuild_org 417ms->3,864ms, rebuild_program 588ms->4,805ms across 20k->160k, unchanged)
test_cases.objective: Verify the rewritten SQL-aggregation rebuild functions hold a flat, table-size-indexed duration budget across >=2 measured table sizes, so the perf test catches a growth-curve regression instead of measuring an empty table.
preconditions: Real test-Postgres migrated to head (migrated_db fixture)
usage_events seeded to at least two of the three measured sizes (20k, 40k, 160k total rows) with realistic program/user distribution matching docs/research/ING-02.md's seed shape
Named per-size budget constants set per /arh-plan-implementation's measurement-derived value (Decision log 'Budget deferral'); EVENT_COUNT=5000 / BUDGET_SECONDS=2.0 removed from the test file
perf_counter + _percentile helper reused per the existing tests/perf/test_range_pagination_perf.py convention

test_data.budget_ceiling_note: rebuild's share of ING-02 p95 <= 3s @ 5000-row batch (sourced); per-size budget constant value itself is set at /arh-plan-implementation, not pinned here

steps: Seed usage_events to the first measured size (e.g. 20,000 total rows) across multiple programs
Run rebuild_org_rollups() and rebuild_program_rollups(program_id), recording duration_ms via perf_counter for each
Assert each duration is within its pinned per-size budget constant
Grow usage_events to the second measured size (e.g. 160,000 total rows) without truncating the first size's rows
Re-run rebuild_org_rollups() and rebuild_program_rollups(program_id), recording duration_ms again
Assert each duration is within its pinned per-size budget constant for the larger size
Compute the growth ratio between the two measured sizes' durations and assert it stays flat (bounded, not linear/super-linear with table size) rather than tracking the pre-rewrite baseline growth
expected_results: Both rebuild_org_rollups and rebuild_program_rollups complete within their per-size budget constant at every measured size
Duration growth between the smallest and largest measured size does not scale with total table size the way the pre-rewrite baseline did (417ms->3,864ms / 588ms->4,805ms)
The test fails (not skips) if a future change reintroduces per-event materialisation and duration tracks table growth again
EVENT_COUNT=5000 / BUDGET_SECONDS=2.0 constants are absent from the test file; assertions are indexed to table size only
